title: AI Assistant for Fisheries Electronic Monitoring
summary: An AI assistant that works alongside human reviewers of at-sea video — helping them cover more footage and miss less.
details: An ongoing collaboration on human–AI teaming for fisheries electronic monitoring. The system supports the people who review long hours of at-sea video, helping them move faster while catching more of what matters. The method and results are written up in a paper currently under review, so I'm keeping the details light for now.

title: Task-Aware Anonymization Framework
summary: A task-aware anonymization framework that hides identity while preserving the cues downstream vision tasks depend on.
details: A task-aware anonymization framework for video: it removes personally identifying information while preserving the motion and appearance cues that downstream tasks — like action recognition — rely on. The goal is perception that can run in privacy-sensitive settings without trading away analytical performance. Ongoing research.

title: Robust Video Understanding for Harsh Marine Environments
summary: Perception methods resilient to occlusion, weather, lighting and motion blur.
details: A line of work on making video-understanding models hold up in the conditions that break them in practice: spray and occlusion, rapidly changing weather and lighting, and severe motion blur from vessel movement. The focus is on reliability and graceful degradation for real maritime deployments rather than benchmark-only accuracy.

title: TubeLite
summary: Lightweight multi-actor spatio-temporal action detection — no heavy transformers or optical flow.
details: TubeLite localizes actors spatially and identifies temporal action boundaries without relying on heavy transformers or optical flow. It builds stable actor tubes with temporal consistency at both the spatial and semantic levels, pairing actor detection with Gaussian-weighted ROI feature extraction and short-term actor-wise temporal propagation. It improves over comparable methods by 4.5 and 7.1 percentage points on two benchmarks while using substantially fewer parameters and FLOPs than transformer-based alternatives. First-author work accepted to ICPR 2026 (arXiv:2607.04684).

title: TrapCounter
summary: Detection, tracking and optical-flow pipeline for automatic counting of active fishing traps.
details: TrapCounter combines object detection, multi-object tracking and optical flow to automatically count active fishing traps as they are deployed and hauled. The pipeline is robust to camera motion and harsh marine lighting and has been deployed in an industry setting. First-author work published at CRV 2025.

title: Discard Action Detection
summary: Real-time motion-aware detection of rare discard events in commercial fishing footage.
details: A motion-aware detection system that identifies rare and visually subtle discard events in long hours of commercial fishing video. It is built for real-time operation on at-sea hardware, handling class imbalance, occlusion and noisy maritime conditions to support catch monitoring and compliance.
